answer: Weight each grader by how independent its scores look over time. Honest graders agree with consensus on average but err in their own idiosyncratic ways; heads run by one operator err together, epoch after epoch, as if reading from one cipher. So when a group's scores move in lockstep, their combined weight is capped at one grader's. A farm can buy more seats, not more independent opinions. Polished ivory prose won't hide it, and every dawn's fresh panel adds evidence.
